questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To become better at German, which is my third language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have had the best six month both personally and academically

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, the intro days at the university of Freiburg were very informative

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A zoom meeting with all the practical stuff, a welcome day and a great ESN whatsapp group with all the social intiatives

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing via the SWFR was amazing and easy. I have lived in a new and nice apartment and been very satifyed with my accmondation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Finding housing outside the SWFR is difficult, but facebook and social media is helpful to find flatmates

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult to find out how to enrol for courses, and the fact that as a master student you could enrol for bachelor courses even though we couldn't actually take part in the course. Further, it was confusing, that you could get different amount of ECTS for the same course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The online registration was also difficult to use and navigate. I have been signed on 10 different courses and signed off most of them again. However, my Erasmus coordinator was very nice and helpfull

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes, I have had help from my erasmus coordinator multiple times - both for signing on to course and signing up for exams

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make the platform HisinOne more accessible for students to use

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was not offered that many political science courses in english. Maybe student should be informed about this or required a certain level of german before coming to freiburg

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The master course was one of the best course I have had during my time in the university. I took one german course that was a little basic but everything was in german so challenging enough

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More student engagement than in Copenhagen, and more demanding paperwork at the end

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Normdynamiken in den Internationalen Beziehungen
Escaping (Un-)Democratic Deadlock
Coloniality, capital, contestation: the political economy of the REG
‘Global South’

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Coloniality, capital, contestation: the political economy of the REG
‘Global South’. The best course and professor in my six years of studying
